hook: Governments are currently restoring 252 million hectares of nature across 149 countries.

sections.voiceover: Governments are currently restoring 252 million hectares of nature across 149 countries.
sections.visual_cue: Animated globe highlighting global restoration zones

sections.voiceover: On October 29, 2026, the United Nations Environment Programme released its first comprehensive stocktake of these efforts. How much of this work happens on land?
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of the United Nations Environment Programme report cover
b_roll: UNEP report document on a desk

sections.voiceover: Out of that total global effort, 232 million hectares involve land restoration specifically.
sections.visual_cue: Data visualization showing land versus total restoration

sections.voiceover: Doreen Robinson describes this as the largest documented restoration effort in history. Each hectare represents a step toward bringing ecosystems back to life.
sections.visual_cue: Portrait of Doreen Robinson next to restoration data

sections.voiceover: Nature is recovering across 252 million hectares of our planet.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of a healthy, restored landscape
b_roll: Panoramic landscape of restored green valley
